#2055. Chelsea co-sporting director Laurence Stewart to leave in leadership reshuffle

Gary Gowers is a sports journalist and the editor of Read Everton, where he leads daily coverage of Everton news, transfers and analysis. He also writes about Manchester City for Read Man City and motorsport for Read Motorsport. A former accountant, he became a freelance writer in 2011 and has written for BBC Sport and Metro.

Laurence Stewart is set to leave Chelsea by mutual consent after almost four years at Stamford Bridge, with the club opting to redistribute his responsibilities rather than appoint a direct replacement.

The departure is understood to be amicable and won’t take immediate effect. Stewart could continue attending matches before formally leaving, following discussions with co-owner Behdad Eghbali over the club’s evolving sporting structure.

The story was first reported by Matt Law of The Telegraph and Nizaar Kinsella of BBC Sport, with Ben Jacobs subsequently providing further details about how Chelsea intend to operate.

Stewart arrived from Monaco in October 2022 as technical director before becoming co-sporting director alongside Paul Winstanley in February 2023.

Chelsea’s day-to-day sporting leadership will now be shared between Winstanley, Sam Jewell and Joe Shields, each with defined responsibilities.

Winstanley will continue overseeing transfer negotiations, player contracts and several departments at Cobham, including medical and performance operations. Shields’ work centres on the academy and player pathways, while Jewell has wider responsibilities across the BlueCo operation, including Strasbourg.

According to Jacobs, discussions about restructuring began in April and accelerated following the appointment of Xabi Alonso as head coach.

Stewart had overseen investment in Chelsea’s data analysis operation, although Jewell and Shields have increasingly taken responsibility for using that information in recruitment and talent identification.

Dave Fallows will remain involved in an advisory capacity, rather than taking on a fixed day-to-day portfolio.

The changes are being described as a natural evolution of Chelsea’s sporting model. There is no suggestion that Stewart’s departure followed a breakdown in relations, and the club are not currently planning to recruit a replacement.

Manchester United could make an ambitious move for former Liverpool sporting director Michael Edwards, with the Glazer family reportedly keen to bring the highly rated executive to Old Trafford.

According to a report from popular Indykaila News on X, the Glazer side of United’s ownership wants Michael Edwards to take full control of the club’s football operations.

With the Glazers interested in the appointment, such a move would be a major shift from the current arrangement at Old Trafford, where Sir Jim Ratcliffe and INEOS are currently responsible for overseeing the football department.

Edwards is regarded as one of the most influential executives in modern English football, having played a major role in building Liverpool’s squad under Jurgen Klopp.

Michael Edwards joined Liverpool in 2011 before being appointed as their sporting director in November 2016. He oversaw player recruitment bring in some of the biggest names at Liverpool including Mo Salah and Sadio Mane. Liverpool saw one of their most successful years in modern history in the Premier League and Europe under Jurgen Klopp while Edwards oversaw the footballing operations.

Manchester United have previously attempted to bring Edwards to Old Trafford before, but were unsuccessful.

Following his departure from Liverpool in 2022, Edwards turned down approaches from several clubs, including Manchester United and Chelsea. He then returned to Fenway Sports Group in March 2024 to oversee FSG’s wider football operations.

His second spell with FSG came to an end in July 2026. That exit has reopened the door for many interested clubs including Manchester United. However, there is no confirmation that Edwards is considering another move to United.

#2052. RIATH AL-SAMARRAI: I'm told control over transfers was key to Mauricio Pochettino taking Man United job. It seems they finally have a manager bullish enough to hold Sir Jim Ratcliffe and Jason Wilcox to account

Published: 21:00 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 09:10 EST, 14 November 2026

It only happened once. But if you search for it, there is footage. The date was February 23, 2000 and the place was the old Wembley Stadium. England 0-0 Argentina, the kind of friendly best forgotten, except for a single line of trivia.

Of all the games played by Jason Wilcox and Mauricio Pochettino, this was the sole example of them sharing a pitch. Wilcox was given the full 90 at a point when Kevin Keegan was low on options for the left wing and Pochettino came on with 35 minutes on the clock and kicked a few people.

He was good at kicking people, Pochettino. He flattened Paul Scholes once, then he nudged over David Beckham and twice he got stuck into Emile Heskey. But Wilcox was in a safe zone on the other side of the field that night. While Pochettino indulged his hobby, Wilcox kept out of harm’s way.

We might ask at this juncture if either of them ever changed their spots. But it’s more interesting to ponder what comes next, now they have been pitched together again at Manchester United.

United needed a big bull to replace Michael Carrick and they have got one. Wilcox’s preference? Well, United’s director of hopeless football quite fancied Eddie Howe, according to the whispers, and Howe is far from a shrinking violet, but he’s not Pochettino. And Pochettino certainly isn’t Carrick.

Pochettino won’t drive to work for three days straight while knowing his race is run. And he won’t have the same patience for incompetence from those below or above.

Manchester United needed a big bull to replace Michael Carrick and they have got one in Mauricio Pochettino

Pochettino is not the sort of manager to drive to work for three days straight while knowing his race is run, like Carrick did this week

With any luck, United knew this when they reached an agreement that was a decade in the making. If they did, it would demonstrate some self-awareness at last, because United have badly needed the right blend of bruiser and diplomat in that seat.

They have cried out for someone who isn’t too nice, too loyal, too whiny or too undermined by their own shortcomings to have the kind of rucks that are needed for change. By that logic, United may have invited their own worst enemy to dinner, or their best chance of a solution.

There have been few managerial appointments in recent years as inherently fascinating as this one. That instinct is partly driven by the thought it has all arrived a touch late – when United favoured Ole Gunnar Solskjaer to replace Jose Mourinho, it was a sliding-door moment for all parties.

But there’s another way of viewing this and that comes from the opposite angle. Maybe this is the perfect time, based on the qualifications needed to operate within the modern version of United.

There is no doubt that Pochettino has lost some of his sheen since his masterful handling of Daniel Levy at Tottenham, but what did he gain? He managed the vastest collection of footballing egos at PSG, worked under a convoluted tier of meddlers in the madhouse of Chelsea and was confronted by presidential interference in his time with the US national team at the World Cup.

Two schools of thought can exist here. One is that he failed to tear up any trees in each of those assignments. But the other talks to the point we are making: United require a manager who can navigate their unique brand of chaos and the new guy knows the dance.

Pochettino won’t ever thank Donald Trump for the Folarin Balogun fiasco in the summer, but Sir Jim Ratcliffe would have to work awfully hard to cause him a more uncomfortable press conference.

The scale of Pochettino’s challenge is obvious. In the micro, that means applying a playing style built on hard running to a squad that jogged its way to embarrassing statistics under Carrick. In the macro, it will be his challenge with Wilcox and a recruitment team that effectively cost Carrick his job.

Pochettino has had plenty to deal with as USA coach, not least the meddling of Donald Trump

Pochettino has the authority to challenge (above, from left) Sir Jim Ratcliffe, Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox over United's failing transfer policy

Talking to one of Pochettino’s former colleagues on Friday, the expectation is that greater control over transfers will have been a key tenet of those negotiations with United.

As predictable as that might sound, it was a huge bone of contention for him at Chelsea and United’s failures in this area are clear. Time will tell if any promises are honoured.

But Pochettino has got what he wanted and pursued. His desire for the post has never been disguised, which can be mapped as a trail of breadcrumbs from that bottle of red he once shared with Sir Alex Ferguson all the way up to carefully planted mentions of the club in gatherings with media.

There were some acts of reassurance necessary for the final step, of course, and doubtless it will sting to leave the US - his farewell tears on Friday showed as much. But not enough to inspire a second thought.

To look back over Pochettino’s other stints in England, one main memory stands out from his time at Tottenham and I’ve cited it in this space previously.

It traces to September 2016, when Pochettino was on the rise and had a game approaching against Pep Guardiola’s Manchester City. In attempting to coax a decent line in the press conference, a few of us killed time before his arrival by digging up old footage of Pochettino’s Espanyol beating Barcelona, when he and Guardiola were on opposing sides.

Within the clip was an unexpected gem, because Pochettino murdered the Brazilian Ronaldo in a challenge. He took the ball, sure, but demolished the man, too, and his boot ended up shoulder-high. We were watching this when Pochettino wandered over and requested a replay – when it was shown, he laughed maniacally.

As a player, he always saw the value in a good reducer. And it’s a trait that might well be needed at United. If Wilcox and the other cronies upstairs don’t up their game, they might find that Carrington offers fewer hiding places than the old Wembley.

Pochettino's fondness for the USA job was apparent by his farewell tears on Friday

Was Tom Brady ever in the Blues' building?

Tom Brady has left Birmingham, but was he ever really there? Across three years, he attended only four games.

The club is on a steep upward trajectory and there is no doubt that the Brady association helped on their commercial side.

But I recall speaking to one Blues shareholder a couple of seasons back, and after attempting to establish some tangible detail about their star investor’s contribution, there was a period of silence. When I asked how often Brady might dial into meetings, there was laughter.

In this era of celebrity ownership of our football clubs, it’s easy to get blinded by a famous name. And easier still to get drawn in by suggestions of expertise that they have carried over from a different space.

But in the vast majority of cases, they are little more than mascots without the costume.

Tom Brady makes a rare appearance at a Birmingham match in 2025

Great delivery from Cummins - but it's not over yet

Pat Cummins stood for 70 minutes on Thursday and answered questions about Sandpapergate.

The Australia captain refused to budge, both from the microphone and his position that Usman Khawaja was incorrect in his claim that the entire team was in on the plot to cheat against South Africa in 2018.

It’s hard to know what was more impressive – Cummins’ commitment to answering every question, or his delusion in believing that it would be the last time he discusses it.

#2047. Is Mauricio Pochettino’s job at Manchester United the toughest in the Premier League?

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United hired Mauricio Pochettino as their next manager to replace Michael Carrick, who managed just one win in 10 games.

His appointment makes him Manchester United’s eighth permanent manager since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013.

Pochettino brings considerable Premier League experience after previous spells with Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea. He has also managed Paris Saint-Germain before the USA job.

As he faces Liverpool for his first game on Sunday, the question arises: is he facing the toughest job in the Premier League?

The question was posed on BBC Radio about who is going to have more pressure, Pochettino or Thomas Frank at Crystal Palace.

According to former Premier League defender Nedum Onuoha, the expectations surrounding Manchester United will make the Argentine’s job considerably harder.

Pochettino is preparing for his first game in charge of Manchester United, with Liverpool waiting at Anfield on November 22. However, the challenge facing the new manager goes beyond getting results on the pitch.

Onuoha believes Pochettino will have to deal with constant discussion and criticism about his work, much of it coming from former United players who are now in the media.

Choosing between Pochettino and Frank, Onuoha said, “Probably Pochettino, because every former Manchester United player works in the media, so there will always be discussion around what he is doing.

“Whereas Frank can just enjoy playing his football at Crystal Palace. If he does well then it is great, if he doesn’t do well then it is still OK.

“But from Pochettino’s perspective, if Manchester United finish the season 15th in the Premier League, whether we like it or not, there will be some criticism of him because he’s had 28 games to do something.”

The comments just highlight the difference in expectations at the two clubs. Frank may have more freedom to work without the same level of attention, while Pochettino will be judged from day one against the standards historically associated with Manchester United. That is one big problem for Pochettino.

Rory Smith from The Observer highlighted another glaring problem at United.  Highlighting a major problem, Smith said, “there is a cycle element to Manchester United whereby a manager comes in, makes things a bit better, and then within a year to 18 months they aren’t challenging for titles again because the Premier League has changed since they were a dominant force.”

Pochettino’s first taste of action as a United manager will be against Liverpool at Anfield on November 22. That opening fixture will give him an immediate test, but the bigger task will be to get back United to winning ways, step by step.

Will the Manchester United job be without pressure for Mauricio Pochettino? Absolutely Not.

#2045. Arsenal face January dilemma as Liverpool and Chelsea join Alex Scott transfer race

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal have made contact with Bournemouth over a potential move for Alex Scott. Mikel Arteta may have to rethink his transfer plans if competition for the midfielder intensifies.

According to The i Paper, Arsenal, Liverpool and Chelsea have all made exploratory enquiries about the 23-year-old. The clubs want to establish what it would take to persuade Bournemouth to sell. However, none appears close to agreeing to a deal.

Arsenal are believed to be keen on a summer move. Liverpool and Chelsea are more interested in signing Scott in January. However, if they were to make a serious offer, it could be hard to hold out.

Scott has become one of the most exciting midfielders in the Premier League. He is an attractive option for clubs looking to improve their squad going forward due to his age, experience and being a homegrown player.

However, there is some uncertainty around Scott’s future. The England international has turned down two contract offers and is unwilling to sign a new deal. There are 18 months left on Scott’s contract, meaning it is an increasingly important decision for Bournemouth.

Arsenal are interested in Scott with doubts surrounding their own midfield options. There have been reports linking Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino to exits.

Scott would give Arteta another option, but Arsenal will have to consider if they want to make a move and give Liverpool and Chelsea an advantage.

Bournemouth are reported to want more than £100m to let him go during the January transfer window.

It would be a big asking price, especially given that Scott has 18 months left on his contract. There are a few reasons why Bournemouth could be holding out for a big fee.

The Cherries had to pay £25m to bring Scott in from Bristol City, who will receive 20 per cent of any future transfer fee. They will also have to find a suitable replacement at the halfway stage.

Reports said Chelsea received a number of offers worth around £70m in the summer, but Bournemouth have rejected claims that a bid of £80m will get them talking.

Scott is believed to be happy to stay at the club until the end of the campaign. Bournemouth are also having a great season under Marco Rose, currently sitting in seventh place in the Premier League with eight straight wins in all competitions.

Arsenal have little to hurry into any deal and could use the summer to negotiate a better deal. This is especially true with Scott’s contract situation becoming more of an issue.

The problem is that Liverpool and Chelsea are keen competitors and could lead to a bidding war in January, leaving Arsenal with little room to negotiate.

Whilst Arsenal have made their interest known, this doesn’t necessarily mean he will be moving anytime soon. If Scott is a genuine target, then they must be prepared to pounce if the situation arises.

Viktor Gyökeres has put to bed any doubts over his future at Arsenal by stating his desire to stay.

The striker has been under question over his long-term future under Mikel Arteta after a difficult start to the 2026/27 season. His latest comments suggest he will not be seeking a move away from north London.

Gyökeres moved to Arsenal for £63.5m from Sporting Lisbon last summer. He’s played a key role in the club winning the Premier League last season with 14 league goals.

However, he has not featured as much this season. Kai Havertz often being Arteta’s go-to man centrally, resulting in him only starting once in the Premier League.

This has led to some speculation that the Sweden international may look at his options in January. However, his latest interview with the Swedish outlet Fotbollskanalen suggests otherwise.

Gyökeres was asked if he wants to stay at Arsenal and has made it clear he wants to continue his career at the Emirates.

The striker also spoke about his relationship with Arteta.

He explained that they regularly discuss football, the team’s approach and the opposition. Those conversations also help him understand what Arteta expects when he is selected to start.

It is a key point to note that just because he hasn’t had much time on the pitch doesn’t mean there have been any issues between the two.

Gyökeres has begun to show his worth again in recent weeks. He found the net against Fleetwood in the League Cup and then Slavia Prague in the Champions League.

#2043. Cardinale says MSE will give Milan ‘financial muscle’ and reiterates: “I will never sell”

Gerry Cardinale has commented on the launch of AC Milan’s new holding company, Milan Sports & Entertainment (MSE), stating that he will never sell the club.

Yesterday, it was confirmed that RedBird had launched the new holding company to ‘consolidate RedBird’s Milan-based investments in sports, infrastructure, and entertainment’. From the new stadium to the NBA Europa project, there are big plans for the company.

Brett Yormark has been appointed as the CEO of MSE after impressing as the Commissioner of the Big 12 Conference (college sports), labelling it ‘an honour’ to get the position. It doesn’t mean that we will see less of Cardinale though, quite the opposite.

In an interview with Gazzetta dello Sport this morning, Cardinale outlined exactly what he wants to achieve with MSE and explained why he will never sell the club. Silvio Berlusconi 2.0, as he calls it, with the goal of taking Milan back to the very top.

Cardinale, what benefits will AC Milan gain from the holding company?

“The driving force behind deals like this is to provide AC Milan with the financial muscle needed to compete in the transfer market and secure the best players in the world.

“I will transform the club’s financial profile with the resources that will come from the stadium, the San Donato Arena, and the other activities we are working on with NBA Europe.

“I’m doing everything I can to ensure that, when we want a player, no one can tell me, ‘You can’t sign him because you can’t afford him.’ Currently, only Premier League clubs are able to invest such sums and secure top players.

“If I want to bring AC Milan back to the top of European competition, not just in Italy, we need to figure out how to compete with the world’s top clubs.”

This project confirms that your commitment to Milan is long-term…

“Yes. I will never sell AC Milan. Never. And this is a project to get them back to winning ways. I’m not willing to tolerate it taking a long time to achieve this. I want to do it as soon as possible. We’ll see how quickly…

“My goal is to consistently win Scudetti and, of course, return to the Champions League. Milan Sports & Entertainment represents the foundation to make all this possible.”

The connection with Milan deserves a separate mention: RedBird and the city are now even more connected…

“This is the legacy we will leave in Milan. The stadium, obviously, represents a huge legacy that will transform our financial profile, but then there’s also the San Donato development project and the rest.

“If we want AC Milan to become great again, we need to close the revenue gap with the Premier League clubs. When I bought the club four years ago, I used the expression ‘Berlusconi 2.0’ and no one understood what I meant. Now perhaps we are starting to see it.”

“Everyone thought I was making an arrogant, self-centred comparison between me and Berlusconi, but that wasn’t my point. What I was trying to explain was that, just as Berlusconi transformed AC Milan and Serie A, we want to be able, through our ownership, to lead the club into a new era.

“We need to do it in the same way Berlusconi did, albeit in a modern way. I’m used to working a certain way because that’s how I do things, at the highest levels worldwide and in America.”

Could your “recipe” also be valid for Serie A?

“Of course, even for Serie A. In my opinion, it wouldn’t have been a good deal to sell 30% of the league’s international TV rights when JP Morgan made that offer. That’s not how Serie A can return to the top of Europe.

“It needs to be done through business planning and by creating every opportunity to generate new revenue. Like we will do with Milan Sports & Entertainment.

“We will be the first to build a stadium since 2011, and that’s a huge achievement. I started working on it when I bought AC Milan, and finally… the right time has arrived.”

Do you think others will follow you on this path?

“No. Some may do it, others may not. We know what it takes to innovate and change. To avoid continuing to practice Einstein’s definition of insanity, according to which everyone wants a different outcome, but doesn’t want to do anything different to get it.”

How long do you think it will take to complete the other projects that will be part of the new holding company?

“I think the NBA is negotiating with the Euroleague, but one way or another, if they can’t reach an agreement, NBA Europe will still launch. Perhaps the first batch of new franchises for Europe will be announced at the end of the year or in early 2027.

“We will see when that happens… We own the land in San Donato, and if I’m granted the Milan franchise, I will be able to start construction fairly quickly because we already have planning permission for a 20,000-seat arena.

“We will also continue to explore opportunities and hold discussions within the tennis world and to organise a tournament in Milan. Finally, we are already making progress in building and launching a hospitality and facility management company.”

Does your plan include organising and managing hospitality services for other clubs’ stadiums as well, not just the new San Siro?

“Yes, the model is the company I created in 2009, called Legends Hospitality. I created it with the New York Yankees and the Dallas Cowboys. Now that company is worth several billion dollars.

“We not only sell premium seats, suites, merchandise, and hospitality, food, and beverage services for Yankee Stadium and Cowboys Stadium, but also for other clubs. I would like to adopt the same model here, probably in partnership with another club.”

Not many football clubs in the world have established an organisation like the one you are leading…

“Exactly. My ambition is to compete with the best clubs in the world. I want to do so thanks to my global vision of the world of sports and entertainment.

“There aren’t many multi-sports platforms in the world that also own some of their own facilities, and we want to add AC Milan to that list. To compete with them and then be better.”

In an effort to generate new revenue, are you also considering a tour for AC Milan next summer? Will that still be Australia or the United States?

“We have already discussed it with Amorim, and I will just tell you that if we play friendlies abroad, they will be in the United States next summer. If we do… We haven’t decided yet, and the decision will be up to Ruben.

“It will depend on what’s best for the team: playing friendlies abroad must add value to the group, not bring in a couple of million for the club. Those extra two million will no longer be our goal, as they were under the previous management. That won’t happen again under this ownership.

“Everything we organise in terms of friendlies will be carefully considered with our coach. Every move. And we won’t participate in tours organised by others. We put our players first. We want to help them prepare well to win. That’s our goal, and we aim to achieve it as soon as possible.”

Welcome to our Live Comments section, where new comments will appear automatically

Cardinale: “i will never sell the club. Support me, we will be together in a long long time.”

He will never sell? We are doomed. He was indeed very arrogant and self-centered when he said that because he’d just arrived, he left Milan to struggle in the summer of ’22 AFTER THE SCUDETTO instead of buying us before September i.e. months before that crucial transfer window which should have been used for a nice upgrade. He was all of that and the time between that interview and now proves it, but one doesn’t have to wait (for) four years to deem such a claim and a statement (as) a VERY RECKLESS one, foolish even. Gerry is right. You are wrong. Look it up.

The English Premiere League makes about FOUR TIMES as much money in TV broadcast rights as Serie A does – €4.6 billion per season (£3.84 billion – £1.68 billion domestic, £2.17 billion international).

Serie A’s TV broadcast rights give it €1.144 billion per season (€894 million domestic, €250 million international)

Total stadium revenue among all the clubs in the English Premier League is also about 2.3 x higher than total stadium revenue for all the clubs in Serie A – over £1billion per season in the EPL (€1.3 billion) compared with €435.4 million per season in Serie A.

It was not always this way. In the 1980s, English football was beset with old, rotting, unsafe stadiums, hooliganism, and low TV revenues.

In 1992, the First Division clubs broke away from the rest of the English Football League (EFL) to form the Premiere League, and began negotiating TV contracts on their own, as well as embarking on a program of enlarging and upgrading their football stadiums. The richest teams began building completely new, large modern stadiums with premium suites, etc.

Meanwhile, nothing much has changed in Italy – most of the stadiums remain municipal owned and small and old.

Ticket prices in the EPL are also generally on average about twice as expensive as in Italy.

So yeah, Serie A had its glory days in the 1990s, as wealthy magnates like Berlusconi infused their personal wealth into their clubs. I remember Fox carried Serie A football on TV in the United States back then. If you wanted to watch the English Premiere League, it was a bit of a struggle to find the matches on TV in the U.S back in the 1990s.

All that changed as the Premiere League steadily built up its international marketing and negotiated ever improved TV contracts. It began to require clubs that were promoted up to the EPL to upgrade their stadiums to meet a certain minimum seating capacity.

And so, today, when Italians complain about how Italy and Serie A can no longer compete with the English Premiere League for the best players, how the EPL hugely overpays for all its star players, the reason is that the EPL makes a $HIT TON MORE MONEY than Serie A does, across the board, in TV income (the biggest factor for the entire league), and stadium income.

That’s why Gerry wanted a new and better stadium, and why he has often talked about Serie A needing to do better marketing and improve its TV contracts.

You can’t get the best players in the world if you can’t compete financially with the richest and most watched football league in the world, which happens to be the English Premiere League right now.

Here in the US, EPL matches are carried by NBC Sports by subscription (about $130-$200 a year). NBC pays the Premiere League $450 million per season to carry English football on TV in the USA.

Serie A matches are carried by Paramount/CBS in the USA (a $90 per year subscription – it went up from $60 after the Ellison Oligarchy mergers). CBS had been paying Serie A $75.8 million per year for those TV rights. However, Serie A with its great marketing and negotiating expertise was unable to improve or renew that contract and so Serie A is currently just going year to year with CBS and getting less than $30 million a year.

Do you see the difference now in the major sources of income between the Premiere League and Serie A??

So yeah, absolutely, Gerry is right to complain about needing to get Serie A some better negotiators and marketers to improve on its TV contracts.

#2042. Jussi Jääskeläinen praises Arsenal star David Raya

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Former Premier League goalkeeper Jussi Jääskeläinen thinks David Raya is the best goalkeeper in the division right now.

But the former Bolton Wanderers star feels the Arsenal No.1 has more to prove before he can be put up with the all-time greats of the competition.

Jääskeläinen recently spoke to Kasinopartio.com, where he praised Raya’s performances and the understanding he has developed with Arsenal’s defenders.

“Raya has been a fantastic signing. He has a great relationship with the centre-backs; even when the back four changes, everything works well.”

The Spaniard has played a key role for Mikel Arteta since his arrival from Brentford. His organisation of the backline, key saves and contribution to Arsenal’s build up play have helped him to be a standout player.

In 2012, Raya began his journey in English football when he moved to Blackburn Rovers from Spain. At that time, he was just a young teenager unfamiliar with English football.

His short spell at Southport introduced him to senior football. Soon, he returned to Blackburn and forged a career ahead of moving to Brentford in 2019. After four years with Brentford, Raya achieved success at the club, helping them to the Premier League.

The player’s performances in the higher leagues caught the attention of Arsenal, and Arteta signed him on loan to the Emirates in 2023 before making the move permanent the following summer.

It didn’t take long for Raya to establish himself in the team. He took home the Premier League Golden Glove, having achieved 16 clean sheets in 32 appearances.

This was a significant milestone in his first season with the Arsenal team, and he has since remained as number one, playing a key role in the club’s pursuit of titles.

While Jääskeläinen said Raya is the best goalkeeper in the Premier League at the moment, he does not think he should be up there with the most experienced.

He believes other goalkeepers have earned an advantage through their consistency over a longer period.

“You have lots of top goalkeepers that I think are still a little bit ahead because of the years they’ve done it in the Premier League.”

“He’s not up there with them yet, but he’s definitely going in the right direction.”

Raya has already proven he can play to the top standard. However, it will be his consistency moving forward that will define his long-term reputation.

Petr Čech, Peter Schmeichel and Edwin van der Sar have all gained great reputations over the years. There is still plenty of time for Raya to do the same, but he will need to keep up his high standards whilst wearing an Arsenal shirt.

At just 31, Raya has a lot left in his career. If he can continue playing at this level, it will make the debate around whether he is one of the best goalkeepers in the Premier League even more intriguing.

#2041. Mikel Merino speaks out on Arsenal role as January rumours grow

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Merino has played down any speculation around his potential exit during January. He has made it clear he will fight to keep his place in the squad.

He also spoke about speculation around Martin Zubimendi, who has been linked with Atletico Madrid.

Both players have been questioned over their role in Mikel Arteta’s midfield. There is increasing competition for positions at the Emirates.

Merino feels that there is always an intense fight for places in top-level football. He spoke about how strong and deep Arsenal are ahead of their Nations League clash against the Czech Republic.

Both Merino and Zubimendi were also keen to stress that they will be looking to gain more opportunities and not get distracted.

Merino has had to adapt to his new role at Arsenal after playing a key role on his team’s side. However, Merino has struggled to get into the starting XI.

He admitted that he wants to play more games. However, he acknowledged that it was difficult to get into the team, as there are so many quality players.

This shows that his playing time has not affected his relationship with Arteta.

Merino was able to understand what it is like to be a manager because his father was a football coach. He understands that tough decisions have to be made when selecting your starting XI.

This can be an important aspect in a difficult season, as all players need to play their part to make sure Arsenal stay challenging in multiple competitions.

Merino’s comments are very interesting considering the uncertainty around Zubimendi.

There are reports Zubimendi has been linked to Atletico Madrid and whether he will be looking to move in January.

Merino didn’t give a definite answer that these players will stay at Arsenal, but the comments do suggest they are looking to improve their position in the squad.

He also underlined the importance of having good cover, with Spain boss Luis de la Fuente believing players coming off the bench can be just as vital as those starting.

This is something Arsenal will want their squad to take on board. They will not always be able to play the same midfielders due to the demands of playing in both domestic and European competitions.

There is still time for Merino and Zubimendi to turn their situation around, so what they are doing now may not indicate how important they are going to be in the campaign.

Arsenal will be keen to keep Merino happy, and he has made his position clear. This should give some reassurance ahead of the January transfer window.

#2040. Arsenal Women vs Barcelona: Arsenal show their resilience with impressive draw against Barcelona

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal Women vs Barcelona: Arsenal Women claimed a vital point at the Camp Nou. They drew 1-1 against Barcelona in the Champions League on Thursday night.

Frida Maanum gave the Gunners the lead in the first half. Caroline Graham Hansen scored to bring the game level after the break. Whilst Renee Slegers will be disappointed to miss out on all three points, her side played some encouraging football.

Despite needing to play differently, Arsenal had an even game against an opposition who would inevitably have long periods of the ball. The visitors played very well defensively and looked dangerous when they could attack.

The result showed that Slegers has a team that can adapt to new challenges. This could be important for Arsenal as they try to make a mark in Europe.

One of the key decisions made by Slegers was to include Maanum. She had only recently returned from injury but made an impressive impact against Barcelona.

The midfielder scored early on to start the game in the right direction. Slegers was very impressed with her play when not in possession. She was praised for her communication skills and assisting others.

Arsenal’s attacking play was mainly based on fast counter attacks. They knew they wouldn’t be able to play in the same style as Barcelona and therefore tried to take advantage of the space on offer.

However, there were chances created in both halves. Arsenal may have been more clinical with their chances, they were always a threat.

Eventually, Barcelona scored their equaliser through Graham Hansen. Slegers said that Arsenal lost their shape during the move, which gave Hansen too much space.

It was a reminder of how quickly Barcelona can strike if you lose your concentration for a moment.

The Arsenal manager was pleased with the way her players implemented the game plan, showing tenacity, discipline, good communication and bravery.

Slegers admitted Arsenal did lose the ball too much in the second half, and by keeping it longer, they would have taken the pressure off defending against Barca’s dangerous attack.

There was some frustration that Arsenal couldn’t hold onto their lead, and there were more chances created towards the end of the game. The visitors got into good positions to win corners but couldn’t get the winning goal.

They will feel very positive from their display. They put themselves up against one of the biggest tests in the Camp Nou and proved that they can cause Barcelona problems.

There isn’t much time to really reflect on the result ahead of their game against the London City Lionesses on Sunday, but Slegers now has another example of what her side can do when they play with purpose and structure.

#2039. West Ham Fans Asked to Unite in Memory of 19-Year-Old Supporter Luke

The loss of a young person reverberates far beyond their immediate family. Today, we are sharing Luke’s story in the hope of raising awareness, encouraging compassion, and supporting a tribute that means so much to those left behind.

Remembering Luke: A Young Life Gone Too Soon

At just 19 years old, Luke’s life was tragically cut short, leaving a family, circle of friends, and wider community struggling to come to terms with an unimaginable loss.

Known affectionately as “Lukey” and “Little Man” by those closest to him, Luke was a devoted West Ham United supporter and a loyal season ticket holder.

As they continue to navigate their grief, Luke’s family have made a simple but heartfelt request.

They are asking West Ham supporters attending the upcoming home fixture against Preston to join together in a minute of applause during the 19th minute of the match, marking the age at which Luke passed away.

The tribute is intended as a celebration of his life and a visible reminder that no family should feel alone during their darkest moments.

A shirt bearing Luke’s name will be placed on his seat in the stadium, providing a poignant symbol of the empty space left by his passing.

By sharing Luke’s story, we hope not only to support his family but also to encourage conversations around loss, grief, and the importance of supporting one another through difficult times.

C&H encourage anyone attending the match, or anyone who sees Luke’s story online, to help spread the word and support the planned tribute.

On the 19th minute, every clap will be a reminder that Luke’s life touched many people and that his memory continues to live on through his family, friends, and fellow supporters.

Our thoughts are with everyone who knew and loved Luke.

If this story resonates with you, please share it to help ensure Luke receives the tribute his family and friends are hoping for. Sometimes the smallest act of support can make the biggest difference.

I have been a season ticket holder since the late eighties, so experienced the highs and lows of being a West Ham supporter. I previously wrote for OLAS and have contributed to a number of football publications in the past.

It proved to be a Tuesday night of late drama for Newcastle United stars involved in Nations League matches.

The final involvement for United players in the November internationals ahead of preparing for Arsenal on Saturday at St James’ Park in the Premier League.

At the Stadion Bilino Polje in Zenica, the versatile Amar Dedic (pictured above) switched from his usual right side to start at left-back for Bosnia & Herzegovina against Romania.

The visitors shocked the home side when taking a sixth minute lead through Birligea.

Takirovic equalised just before the break and then late drama as in the 82nd minute Bajraktarevic got the winner for Bosnia.

Amar Dedic played the full match and that win means that Bosnia & Herzegovina have finished runners-up in Nations League Group H.

Anthony Elanga started on the bench for Sweden away against Poland at the Tarczyński Arena in Wroclaw.

With the score 1-1, the Newcastle winger one of two subs coming on in the 65th minute and Elanga swiftly set up Beijmo but he put his effort over the bar.

That is the way the score remained and it means Sweden topped Group H.

Over in Copenhagen it ended up a five goal thriller between Denmark and Norway.

William Osula started on the bench and saw his Danish teammates go two up within 14 minutes with goals from Hojlund and Hojbjerg.

Haaland then got one back eight minutes before the break and Denmark still led 2-1 when William Osula gained his latest international cap when coming off the bench with 15 minutes remaining.

However, the late drama ended up coming at the other end of the pitch, as Odegaard made it 2-2 in the 83rd minute.

Deep in added time Fulham’s Joachim Andersen handled the ball in the penalty area and up stepped Erling Haaland to score a 96th minute winner from the penalty spot.

That very late winner meant Norway finished runners up in Nations League Group D and Denmark dropped to third.

Alan Shearer believes Ezri Konsa has been the Premier League’s best player this season after an impressive start to his Arsenal career.

But the former Newcastle United striker has been impressed by the Gunners’ backline and feels Konsa should take a large amount of credit for the fact that they have not missed William Saliba so much.

Konsa’s arrival at Emirates has provided Mikel Arteta with a defender, but his performances have caused some issues for the Arsenal boss. Konsa is now a viable option for Arteta to play, as Saliba is fit again.

Shearer feels Konsa has done enough to be regarded as the best player in the division so far.

He stated in the Metro that Konsa has been effective while playing for Arsenal in the defence.

The former Newcastle player believed that Konsa has been the best player in the Premier League during this season. He pointed out the proof of the performance in the defence, arguing that people did not notice the missing Saliba until now.

Konsa has proved just how much he has grown since moving to the Emirates. Arsenal have been very strong at the back with Konsa playing a massive part.

But there is a problem with Konsa’s performances. Even if Saliba is fit he has done more than enough to make his place difficult to take.

Saliba is still one of Arsenal’s most important defenders, so Arteta will be delighted to have him back. However, he can’t ignore what Konsa has done in his absence.

It would be a tough call to leave the Englishman out, as he has been in such great form. But it means an experienced first choice defender would be left on the bench.

#2034. Why England fans booed Arsenal defender Ben White again after Croatia win

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Ben White returned to the England senior squad on Thursday night but received a hostile reception at Wembley.

The Arsenal defender came on as a substitute in the 78th minute of England’s 2-1 Nations League win against Croatia but was met with boos from a section of the crowd.

Thomas Tuchel has since defended White, stating that he should be in the squad. However, this raises questions as to why some England supporters have turned on the defender after he has continued to perform well for Arsenal.

The answer lies with the 2022 World Cup in Qatar.

He did not play in the first two group games for England and missed the last group game against Wales due to illness.

There were reports that White had fallen out with assistant manager Steve Holland, but neither the FA nor England management confirmed this was the reason he left.

Gareth Southgate later stated there were no problems between White and Holland and that White had simply withdrawn himself from selection after the tournament.

This meant that White would never play for England again while Southgate was still manager. Some fans were clearly upset by this, as they felt White was shunning his country.

When White returned under Tuchel in March 2026, he was met with a negative reaction. He was booed by the crowd when he scored his first-ever international goal against Uruguay. White was also booed in the same fashion against Japan.

He has since explained that supporters might view the situation differently if they knew the full story. However, he has chosen not to reveal the private details behind his departure.

Tuchel has shown little concern about White being affected by the controversy.

The England boss said after the win on Thursday that he had not heard any boos and praised White’s qualities, work ethic and desire to play for his country.

He believes White can help England win games and added that he has the backing of the coaching staff.

Arsenal fans will be unsurprised to learn that White is still a valuable asset for Mikel Arteta, offering defensive consistency and being able to play as a right or centre-back.

The bad press that White is receiving from England fans will not go away any time soon. However, he has not done anything to hurt his reputation at club level. The reasons why he left for the World Cup are personal.

The main focus for Arsenal will be getting him match fit again. As for the England fans, we shall see.

#2033. Arsenal Women vs London City Lionesses preview: Gunners face tough test at the Emirates

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal look to build on their recent win over Liverpool as they return to the Emirates Stadium but will face an impressive London City Lionesses side who are a potent attacking threat on their travels.

Renée Slegers’ team have struggled to convert their strong performances into points in the league this season. They have lost their last four WSL games at home, however, becoming the first team in WSL history to draw four successive games at home.

Their bad run must come to an end. They have taken just three points from their first nine league games so far this season, scoring a miserable total of 10 goals. However, they look like they have more in the tank and will need to be much more clinical in front of the goal.

The day also marks Slegers’ 50th game in charge of the WSL. The Dutch manager has only lost six league games so far this season, with only Chelsea having a better record from teams that have been ever-present in the division.

Arsenal can’t take their opposition lightly after London City’s impressive recent form. They have won two and drawn once in their last three away league games, scoring 12 goals.

Eder Maestre’s side has become a potent attacking force. Daniëlle van de Donk has provided four assists this season, and Delphine Cascarino has scored three goals and provided two assists.

Kadidiatou Diani can be dangerous. She has scored or assisted in all four of her league games away from home this season.

London City’s attacking prowess means they are a far different proposition to some teams Arsenal have faced at home. They have been in a positive situation for 62.7 per cent of their league minutes this season, the highest in the WSL.

Arsenal will have to deal with the attacking threats but look to utilise their ball possession better. Giving London City an opportunity to counter could make an already tough afternoon even tougher.

Alessia Russo comes into the game having found the net in her last three WSL games and will be key in converting Arsenal’s chances into goals.

The Gunners also showed their fighting spirit in their midweek clash against Barcelona. They drew 1-1 at Camp Nou to become the first side to take points off the Spanish giants in the Women’s Champions League at home since April 2024.

Slegers’ team will feel emboldened by that result but will have to change their tactics against London City.

They have won all seven games against Arsenal so far, scoring an impressive 22 goals and only conceding once. However, given London City’s recent away form, they will be hotly favoured.

They certainly have the quality to take all three points, but they must finally convert their dominance into a comfortable home win.

#2032. Why Bukayo Saka's England spot is suddenly under threat: Clocking up the miles has made Arsenal star a fitness concern - while his rival Morgan Rogers is hitting top gear: CRAIG HOPE

Published: 08:57 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 09:21 EST, 14 November 2026

Five seasons ago, Bukayo Saka clocked up 3,000 Premier League minutes for Arsenal. Morgan Rogers appeared in just 217 for Bournemouth, then of the Championship. The pair are the same school age. Yet, back then, one was a young man at the very top of the game, the other was a boy wondering where, and how, he would ever get a game.

In the same week that Rogers, a Manchester City junior, made his only league start during an unhappy loan season on the south coast - in a goalless draw at Peterborough - Saka was scoring in a 3-1 win in the North London derby. They were on very different flight paths.

Today, the ascent of Rogers compares with, dare we say it, the gradual descent of Saka. His supporters will contest that trajectory. They can point to his two goals for England in Croatia last month, his hat-trick in the 6-4 World Cup bronze-medal victory over France and, of course, his Premier League winner’s medal. Their argument has merit, as does any that defends a player of such talent.

Except, this is not about ability. It is about durability. It is about mileage and the fear that, at 25 years old, a near 400 career games are weighing heavy. Rogers, quite remarkably, has played 10,000 fewer Premier League minutes. He is, to borrow horse-racing parlance, unexposed and open to improvement.

Until three years ago, this was Saka. He started 87 consecutive Premier League games for Arsenal, a club record, and was getting better season on season - seven, 12, 15 and 20 were his goals tallies from 2021 to 2024. He was both the present and future of the England team.

Bukayo Saka's starting spot in the England XI is now under serious threat ahead of Euro 2028

England are flourishing with Chelsea's Morgan Rogers (right) occupying the right-hand side

And yet now, increasingly among those who obverse and are close to the England camp - including, you suspect, Thomas Tuchel - there is a feeling of Saka’s presumed starting jersey being under serious threat. In fact, you wonder if the threat has already passed. Does the position on the right of England’s forward line, with a view to Euro 2028, now belong to Rogers?

This, it should be said, is as much about the exceptional development of Rogers, who will again start on the right here in Spain on Sunday night. But there is another, more uncomfortable possibility, and that is of Saka’s very best days belonging to those North London derbies of yesterday, not tomorrow. He is currently injured with a thigh strain and faces several more weeks on the sidelines.

I was in the room with Tuchel at the World Cup pre-camp in Florida when he revealed, to some surprise, ’Bukayo is just not there yet. Some things are missing’. We had assumed Saka was fit after arranging private sessions in the wake of the Champions League final. The head coach, however, said it would be ‘very unlikely’ that Saka, nursing Achilles discomfort, would be able to start and finish all of England’s matches, and so it proved. He did not start and finish any before the France kick-about, a match that should have been played at Miami Beach, not Miami Stadium.

In the days prior to the semi-final against Argentina, Saka told Tuchel and medical staff he was ready to start. Tuchel went with Rogers on the right and Saka was an unused substitute. After his treble three days later, Saka spoke of his frustration with his playing time in North America.

Throughout the tournament, Tuchel rejected the idea of the Arsenal man being ‘the saviour’, as it was put to him by one colleague following the group-stage goalless draw with Ghana.

‘I’m not engaging in that,’ he told us. ‘It’s not like Bukayo comes back and everything is solved.’

And Tuchel was right. Saka did a lot of good - three assists in the tournament proper - but it felt like he was existing in moments, much like at Euro 2024. Gone was that whiplash speed taking him through defensive lines, the drag and dribble that defenders knew was coming but could do little about. Club-mate Noni Madueke had that explosion, just not Saka’s end product. Combine the two and we had a player. It was why, come the semis, Tuchel went with Rogers.

Recurring injuries and setbacks have plagued the Arsenal winger over the past few seasons

He was once viewed as England's present and future - but has suffered from a gradual decline

To revisit our Daily Mail Sport tournament ratings, in which Saka scored 6/10, we recorded: ‘Fitness issues should offer some context, but this was a version of Saka unrecognisable from the player we thought was up there with Kane and Bellingham when it came to being a game-changer. He did provide three assists, including a lovely cross for the opener in Mexico, but never appeared to fully trust his body. Has a bit to prove when back to full fitness.’

Will he ever, though, regain a consistent level of fitness, strength and sharpness that allows him to impact - again, consistently - like he once did? Just last week, Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta admitted the club were struggling to identify the underlying reason for injuries which total double figures in three years.

‘We have openly discussed a lot of things with him to understand what could possibly have gone wrong,’ said Arteta. ‘But the reality probably is that unfortunately we don’t know.’

Saka, to return to horse racing, has the form in the book, but that is the concern. There is, perhaps, too much form at too young an age, especially when coupled with a game reliant on acceleration and intensity.

Rogers himself still has a lot to prove, not least because of his £117million transfer from Aston Villa to Chelsea in the summer. With that, though, he has grown. That much was evident by him taking centre stage against Croatia on Thursday night despite the presence of Harry Kane and Jude Bellingham. Previously, you suspected Rogers was waiting for the leading men to hand him his script.

His tendency to come infield will suit Tuchel, too. Kane the quarterback, as we saw at Wembley, leaves a space to populate and exploit. Rogers had more touches in the penalty area than any other player, including the one for his opening goal. And if Anthony Gordon, on the opposite flank, is the one with chalk on his boots, Rogers muddying his in the goalmouth is what the team needs.

Meanwhile, Rogers has hit top gear at Chelsea and become a key man under Thomas Tuchel

This debate, Saka versus Rogers, is not one that should keep Tuchel awake at night. It is a nice problem to have - the hope that Saka will return to his best, the expectation that Rogers is still to realise his.

On Sunday, at the Metropolitano Stadium in Madrid, Rogers has another opportunity to further his claims. He has come a long way since a drab Wednesday night at Peterborough’s London Road in 2021. It is, though, the distance yet travelled that is most exciting.

#2030. Premier League Key Match Incidents panel has ruled on two Newcastle United incidents

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

The Premier League Key Match Incidents Panel has now given its verdict on two match moments concerning Newcastle United.

The KMI panel has five members, made up of three former players and/or coaches, plus one representative each from the Premier League and PGMOL (Now ‘Pro Ref’).

It was set up at the start of the 2022/23 season to give an independent assessment of decision-making rather than relying on the views of PGMOL or the clubs themselves.

The judgement is intended to provide an arm’s-length assessment of all major match incidents but gives weight to the decision of the referee in subjective situations.

Taking into account the laws of the game and the Premier League’s interpretation.

The Premier League Key Match Incidents Panel have looked at the Fulham v Newcastle United match that was played on Saturday 17 November 2026 and voted on these two incidents.

On 33 minutes: Dan Burn goal disallowed by the referee because of a challenge by Yoane Wissa on Timothy Castagne. The Var not asking the referee on the pitch to review his decision.

KMI Panel: Panel voted 5-0 in support of the referee’s decision.

KMI Panel: Panel voted 5-0 in support of the VAR decision not asking the referee to review.

‘Why was the goal disallowed? In this instance, it was deemed that Wissa was committing an offence by making a holding action on Castagne, which was both a clear attempt to manipulate the offside line and create free passage for Burn to play the ball into goal without any challenge from Castagne. One of the Refereeing Points of Emphasis for the 2026/27 Season includes holding offences, with referees enhancing recognition of clear holding actions that have clear material impact, and/or non-footballing holding actions with no place on a football pitch.’

The Premier League Key Match Incidents Panel also reviewing another moment in that Fulham v Newcastle United match:

On 74 minutes: Fulham claiming a penalty for an incident involving Dan Burn and Berge in the box.

KMI Panel: Panel voted 5-0 in support of the referee’s decision.

KMI Panel: Panel voted 5-0 in support of the VAR decision not asking the referee to review.

The Premier League Key Match Incidents Panel explaining: ‘The referee’s call of no penalty was supported. The contact by Burn was deemed to be below the threshold for a foul as Berge lost some of his balance as he tried to change direction to follow the ball.’

#2029. Arsenal transfer interest in Alphadjo Cisse: Arsenal face a £50m decision as AC Milan youngster attracts Premier League interest

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal transfer interest in Alphadjo Cisse is starting to take shape. Arsenal are monitoring the development of AC Milan starlet Alphadjo Cissé, although his sensational start to the season could prove to be costly for Mikel Arteta.

The 20-year-old has made a blistering start to his Serie A career and attracted interest from a number of Premier League clubs after his impressive displays so far. Arsenal are reported to be interested.

The Gunners are among several clubs, including Brighton, keeping tabs on the player, according to Italian football news website Tuttomercatoweb. The striker is rumoured to be worth up to 60 million euros. That’s an eye-watering sum for a player who is just starting out in his professional career.

Cissé was signed by Milan from Hellas Verona in February 2026 but was allowed to finish the season on loan at Catanzaro.

Prior to joining the San Siro, he had already showcased his potential with six goals in 22 games in Serie B. He has made a huge impact since moving up to the top division.

Cissé has found the net five times in nine Serie A games this season. He has also chipped in with three goals in four Europa League games, making a total of eight goals in 13 games.

This has made him an important addition to the Milan squad. He is also versatile, as he can play as an attacking midfielder or higher up the park.

Arsenal may find his versatility attractive. Arteta likes players who can play in different positions and with injuries, and with a busy fixture list, he will want to have players who can do that.

The main issue could be that Milan are keen to keep their young star.

It is reported that the Italian club have turned down a verbal offer from Brighton and are looking to extend Cissé’s contract, which currently runs until June 2030.

This indicates that Milan is considering his future, rather than looking to make a profit. It also demonstrates just how quickly his reputation has developed.

Arsenal have the funds to target exciting young talent, but would they want to spend so much on Cissé?

There is no indication that he would be an instant replacement for Arsenal’s current attacking options. However, Cissé’s age, goal-scoring ability and versatility make him an interesting prospect.

This could be one to keep an eye on beyond January. Milan have little motivation to sell, and Arsenal might want to see how he develops before committing themselves.

Cissé has already hit the ground running in Italy and now needs to prove that his initial success can turn into something more consistent.

#2027. Max Dowman breaks Jude Bellingham record as Arsenal teenager makes England history

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Max Dowman has added another incredible achievement to his burgeoning career after becoming the youngest player to play for the England Under-21s.

The Arsenal youngster was introduced from the bench in Friday’s 1-0 friendly loss to Portugal at Ashton Gate. The 16-year-10-month-13-day-old player is over three months younger than Jude Bellingham was when he played his first game for the Under-21s.

Dowman replaced former Arsenal academy player Amario Cozier-Duberry in the 61st minute. He came on alongside debutant Trey Nyoni as England tried to shift the momentum of a challenging game.

An early strike from Afonso Moreira gave Portugal the lead in the 28th minute. An ineffective England team failed to respond. However, the replacements gave Lee Carsley’s team some late momentum.

Despite the hosts’ attempts to level the score, they failed to break down the Portuguese defence. The result means England have lost for the second game running. However, Dowman had much to be pleased with personally.

Dowman has added to his growing collection of records.

He became the youngest player to play in the Champions League, the youngest goalscorer in the history of the Premier League and the youngest to win the Premier League title.

Breaking Bellingham’s England Under-21 record is another significant step. It shows how quickly Dowman has progressed through the international age groups.

He has already made a big impression at Arsenal with Mikel Arteta’s love of giving younger players a chance, but Dowman will have some stiff competition for first team minutes.

Another positive is his progression on an international scale. He will improve both physically and tactically playing against older players and gain experience at a higher level.

England will host France in their next friendly on Monday, 16th November. Dowman will be hoping to feature after his instant impact on the record books.

Despite the disappointing result against Portugal, it was a landmark evening for the Arsenal players.

Dowman is already building a legacy at club level, but now he can add to his list of records by becoming an England Under-21 record holder.

At just 16, he has plenty of time to improve and show consistent performances to get more opportunities with the senior Arsenal squad.

#2026. Writing’s on the wall for West Ham stalwart’s international career

Time catches up with all of us, footballers just the same. Few are given much indication that the writing is on the wall, until suddenly that place which was automatically theirs is going to a younger, fitter, faster team mate – and then, suddenly, without a fanfare, almost always without even a ‘thank you’ –  it is over.

That, sadly, is likely to be the outcome for Czech stalwart and former captain Tomas Soucek who found himself an unused substitute last night after appearing for just five minutes in his countries’ previous game – during which Tornado Tom’s mistake in added time gifted Spain the injury time second goal in their 2 – 0 defeat of the Czechs.

A total of 93 appearances – 42 as captain – and nineteen goals is a pretty stellar international career and for Soucek to have fought his way back from such a bad injury at the World Cup last summer shows his fighting spirit.

You’d think it unlikely that Soucek will make the squad in the March window, after being virtually discarded for the two Nations League games just gone – both of which his Czech Republic side lost.

Hopefully it’ll give the veteran a little more gusto to complete the job and see his West Ham side over the line and promoted back to the Premier League – which would be a fitting swan song for Soucek who’d be 32 next season and probably a bit-part player if the Hammers make it back to the top tier.

At least it’d mean domestically, he could go out at the top. Which he thoroughly deserves after more than 250 West Ham caps.

I still watch YouTube repeats of the Cup Final of 2006 hoping in vain that Shaka Hislop grows another six inches and stops Steven Gerrard's injury time equaliser. Can tell I'm getting old knowing I watched both Mark Noble's debut and his last game at West Ham. Pulling on a Claret and Blue replica shirt still makes me feel the same butterflies as when I was seven years old. Magic.

Nothing lasts forever. Tomas has an international career to be proud of, the envy of many.

Tad early to write him off at the end of this season, though. Tomas will decide when it is time for him to give it all up.

We have done well out of him during his prolonged spell with us.

#2025. Martin Ødegaard sends clear message to Arsenal amid Bayern Munich transfer rumours

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Martin Ødegaard has spoken out about the speculation surrounding his future. He has stated he would like to stay at Arsenal for the future.

The captain has also admitted that talks about a new deal have not yet begun. Ødegaard is currently under contract until the summer of 2028. This leaves Arsenal with an important decision to make over the coming months.

Bayern Munich are being linked with an interest in the midfielder according to reports from Germany. The Bundesliga giants are said to be keeping their eyes on the player’s situation.

Speaking while on international duty with Norway, Ødegaard was quick to dismiss the speculation. He made it clear he is settled in north London and sees his future being at the Emirates Stadium.

There is no suggestion that the 27-year-old is seeking a move. Although comments do highlight a contract issue that Arsenal will be keen to resolve in the short term.

The Norwegian’s laid-back attitude should be encouraging for supporters.

He has made it clear that he is happy at the club and wants to stay here for the time being. This means that there is no need to panic.

However, Arsenal will have to get him to sign on the dotted line. Leaving his captain in the last year of his contract with no progress would cause an unnecessary distraction.

Since his permanent move from Real Madrid in 2021, Ødegaard has become a key player in Mikel Arteta’s plans. He has grown into a team leader and is one of the most influential players in the dressing room.

His importance has been shown by his inclusion in all 10 of Arsenal’s Premier League games so far this season. He has scored three goals.

This is a big improvement on last season, where he was hampered by injuries and failed to make much of an impact in front of goal.

It wouldn’t be a shock to see Bayern Munich show interest in Ødegaard, but don’t take this as a sign he is close to a move.

There is little reason for Arsenal to consider losing their captain. He brings so much more to the team than just his technical ability and has been relied upon by Arteta to lead by example.

The midfielder was also pivotal in the 1-0 win over Hull City on 7 November, scoring the winner in the 72nd minute to give the league leaders three crucial points.

Arsenal have put themselves in a good position in the title race. Keeping their key players happy will be important in the second half of the campaign.

The Gunners will be focused on their game against Newcastle United on 21st November.

Arsenal fans have no real reason to panic at the moment, with the captain wanting to stay at the club and his comments suggesting he is happy.

However, it would be a good idea for the club to try and ensure his long-term future at the club. Ødegaard is still an important part of Arteta’s strategy, and ensuring he stays at the club would be a smart move.

#2024. Lewis Hall new insight, excelling in central midfield and as a 10 is intriguing to hear

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Lewis Hall was superb for England in the wins over both Croatia and Spain.

The rest of the world suddenly catching up with what Newcastle United fans have said for a long time.

Lewis Hall is an elite talent and he has been proving that for NUFC across recent seasons.

The lifelong United fan is the best left-back England have, as well as being the most talented in the Premier League.

Very amusing to hear so many people in the media going on like they are the ones who have suddenly ‘discovered’ Lewis Hall.

Somebody who has known Lewis Hall for a very long time is Ed Brand.

Brand worked with him when Hall was an emerging talent at Chelsea.

Former Chelsea Under 18s Head Coach Ed Brand declaring to Sky Sports about Lewis Hall: “What a good kid he is. A lot of the time [with the Chelsea Under 18s] I was playing a 3-4-2-1 formation with 10s…I would put him as a 10 quite a bit because he had always been a central midfield player. If I played a 4-2-3-1 formation then I would play him as one of the 6s or the 8s instead.”

Ed Brand going on to explain how Lewis Hall was then asked to play other roles, left wing-back and eventually left-back: “There were players who were older than Lewis Hall, good players, [so] in certain games where I wanted to keep him in the team, he might have to play at left wing-back even though I knew at that point it was not his favourite position. He was a midfielder. I was going to him [ahead of playing in a match against Tottenham], ‘Look, this is how I will fit you in.’ I just wanted 11 footballers in every position because we wanted to make sure we got on the ball. He started to play there a little bit more, a little bit more, and it just went from there. Now he is seen in most football fans’ eyes as a left back. Whereas I know that growing up, he has always been an attacking player with the ability to get goals and run beyond.”

Brand going on to say: “Lewis Hall was excellent when he was a 10. But people adapt and see your football differently. He is so comfortable at left-back because of where he is used to playing. When you are a player with his ability, used to playing in the centre of the pitch, seeing the game 360, you get moved to full-back, you look at it and think it is easy. He can see everything. Full-backs in the modern game are so important with how they invert inside, they do a lot of stuff infield anyway. With his talent, he excels there. What is so impressive about Lew is how much he has improved upon his defensive side. You cannot play in the Premier League and not be able to defend to a certain level, He will continue to get better the more exposure he gets to that.”

My view for a long time has been that Lewis Hall is such a talented player, he could play anywhere on the pitch and excel.

Ed Brand looking to the future and saying: “He has done brilliantly…[and] in time  he will be one of those England internationals whose name will be one of the first on the sheet. I am biased but I already think there is a big enough case for it.”

#2022. Arsenal Women held by London City Lionesses despite Frida Maanum goal

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal Women missed the chance to end their frustrating run of draws at home as London City Lionesses came from behind to earn a 1-1 draw at the Emirates Stadium.

Frida Maanum gave the Gunners the lead in an exciting start to the game. But Isobel Goodwin equalised almost straight away. Despite creating plenty of chances, Renée Slegers’ side failed to find a second goal.

Arsenal have now lost their last five WSL games at the Emirates. The results were yet another frustrating afternoon for the defending champions, who put in a strong display against Barcelona in Europe earlier in the week.

Arsenal started on a high note, creating some dangerous chances with their quick play. Emily Fox and Lisa Baum worked really well together down the right, and Ona Batlle had a great chance from the edge of the box.

As the pressure mounted, Fox surged forward and played a perfectly weighted through ball to Alessia Russo. The striker turned and played the ball back to Maanum, who rounded off her impressive comeback from injury by finishing.

Arsenal had little time to rejoice. London City equalised just a minute later as Goodwin found herself in space to fire past Misa Rodríguez.

The visitors looked more confident after equalising, but Mary Earps was proving a tough ask for Arsenal to score past. The ex-Manchester United shot-stopper kept out Baum and made some key stops from Arsenal’s efforts.

Rodriguez also had to make a key stop before half-time as she got a hand to Daniela Arques Lazaro’s powerful strike to keep the scores level.

The Gunners continued their attacking play but were made to work hard by a high pressing side from London City.

But Arsenal still managed to create some chances. Caitlin Foord put Earps under pressure and Maanum and Baum combined before the latter saw her curl just wide.

London City posed a threat too. With Kadidiatou Diani and Grace Geyoro causing defensive problems for Arsenal, Geyoro fired into the side netting.

Delphine Cascarino had the game’s defining moment of the second half, hitting the crossbar from outside the box. However, Arsenal were lucky to escape and Maanum came close to winning the game, hitting the woodwork from a dangerous counter.

Slegers brought on Kyra Cooney-Cross and Olivia Smith in the 72nd minute to provide some new energy. Smith looked lively upon entering the game, but Earps denied her efforts and Batlle’s cross.

Emily Fox had to be substituted due to injury in the final moments of the game, but Slegers later indicated that she would be okay.

The Gunners were unable to find a winning goal and will now turn their attention to their Champions League clash on Thursday with Lyon. They will then face West Ham at home in the WSL.
